transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-04-11 14:00 UTC
- Duration: ~68 minutes
- Recorded by: Fireflies.ai
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Ruiz (CTO, LabAxis), Samir Khan (Head of ML), Priya Desai (Security), Alex Morgan (Procurement)

Summary:
- Goal: scope a 6-10 week POC to evaluate open-models for structured extraction + summarization across regulatory and clinical text in 5 languages.
- Success criteria discussed: extraction F1 targets, latency p95, throughput, and quality thresholds for multilingual support.
- Shortlist: mix of mid-size and large open models for tradeoff testing (cost vs quality), plus quantized variants for infra sizing.
- Next steps: share bench template, customer to supply labeled sample set, SE to produce model footprint estimates, security checklist to be confirmed.

Topics: success criteria; workload sizing; benchmark metrics (accuracy + latency); multilingual behavior; deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private); data security / SOC2 / KMS; timeline and acceptance criteria.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for carving the time, i'll do a super quick intro—i'm maya from redwood inference, and liam's our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Dr. Elena (LabAxis): hi thanks, excited to see how we can push this into clinical docs, we've got a pile of regulatory submissions and trial notes that we want to extract structured fields from.
[00:16] Samir (LabAxis): yeah hi, objective is twofold: high-precision entity extraction (protocol ids, outcome measures) and short regulatory summaries. multilanguage support is important—spanish, french, german, japanese and chinese for our EU/APAC trial partners.
[00:28] Liam (Redwood SE): perfect. quick clarifying q: are you thinking of a single model that handles both extraction and summarization or separate specialized models?
[00:34] Dr. Elena: we prefer one pipeline but we could do a hybrid—extraction first then a summarizer. the extraction precision is priority.
[00:42] Alex (Procurement): timeline constraints—we've got a board checkpoint in mid-june so would like an initial demo by 2026-06-10 if possible.
[00:50] Maya: ok so ~8-9 weeks, that lines up with a 6-week bench + 2–3 week pilot, sounds doable, we'll propose a phased plan.
[00:58] Priya (Security): quick note: for any PII/sensitive data we need encryption at rest with customer-managed KMS and audit logs. also we will need SOC2 attestation and an NDA in place before sharing data.
[01:10] Maya: understood, we can do private deployment for the pilot or host with VPC peering and customer KMS—liam can walk through options.
[01:18] Liam: right — there's three practical routes: hosted sandboxes (fastest), Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) for consistent throughput, or Redwood Private in your VPC for full control. each has tradeoffs in setup time and cost.
[01:32] Samir: curious about latency SLOs — for extraction we need p95 under 300ms for sub-512 token requests, ideally 200ms. is that realistic?
[01:42] Liam: depends on model size and quantization. smaller 7–13B instruc-style models can hit ~100–200ms p95 with dynamic batching on a high-end A100/NVIDIA 4090 mix, larger 70B+ typically sit higher unless you use quantized int8/in8 or sequence offloading. kv cash and batching — sorry kv cache — helps for chatty flows but less relevant for single-shot extraction.
[02:06] Dr. Elena: you said A100 vs 4090 mix, what's the expected throughput for our workload, we've got peaks around 20 req/s for nightly processing and 5 req/s sustained for interactive analysts.
[02:16] Liam: for stateless extraction at 512 tokens: a single A100 can handle roughly 30–50 r/s on optimized 13B int8 models, for 70B quantized you might hit 6–12 r/s. we'll size pools based on your peak.
[02:28] Maya: right, and part of the POC is to measure cost per thousand tokens and per inference with typical batch settings—reduce unit cost while keeping latency SLO.
[02:36] Samir: ok can we talk models — what's your recommended shortlist for open models that balance quality for clinical/regulatory text and cost?
[02:44] Liam: here's what we suggest to include in the bench:
- Mistral-Instruct 7B (low latency, strong instruction-following for extraction with fine-tuning)
- Llama 2 13B and 70B (classic baseline; 70B for quality ceiling)
- Falcon-40B / 180B variants (good deep domain performance, heavier footprint)
- MPT-30B / Mosaic models optimized for long-context summarization
- A distilled 13–15B candidate (if you want faster throughput)
We'll also test int8 quantized variants and a 4-bit experimental quant to see memory/latency tradeoffs.
[03:20] Dr. Elena: do you have any model that's trained/tuned on biomedical text? open models tend to be generic and might miss domain-specific lexicon.
[03:28] Liam: good call — there are some domain-adapted weights (community forks) and we can also run a short supervised fine-tuning / LoRA pass on your labeled examples during POC. that usually gives the best lift for entity F1.
[03:38] Samir: whats the expected F1 lift from LoRA on ~2k labeled examples? ballpark.
[03:44] Liam: ballpark you might see +5–12 points F1 for extraction tasks depending on label quality. if labels are high-quality, expect the higher end.
[03:52] Priya: on private deployments, what's Redwood's access to logs and are audit logs exportable to our SIEM?
[03:58] Maya: yes, audit logs and per-token traces can be exported via syslog or pushed to your S3 with encryption. private deployment gives you full control over keys; hosted managed still supports customer KMS for encryption but network egress is still managed.
[04:12] Alex: procurement question — cost model for pilot vs production?
[04:16] Maya: for pilot we propose time-and-materials with a capped spend estimate (we'll provide a bench cost sheet); production can be reserved capacity (Dedicated) with committed monthly spend reducing per-token costs.
[04:26] Samir: benchmark metrics — let's define them now so they're measurable.
[04:30] Liam: recommended bench metrics:
- Extraction: precision, recall, F1 by entity type (protocol id, dosage, outcome), macro-F1 overall.
- Summarization: ROUGE-L, factuality checks against gold snippets, and human eval (paired A/B).
- Latency: p50/p95 request latency for 128/512 token inputs.
- Throughput: steady-state r/s under typical batch sizes.
- Cost: $ per 1k tokens and $ per inference with batch settings.
- Failure modes: hallucination rate measured by false-positive extractions.
[04:58] Dr. Elena: for multilingual evaluation we need per-language slice metrics and confusion matrices.
[05:02] Liam: absolutely, we'll run per-language bench sets, if you can provide labeled data per language it'll be most meaningful; otherwise we'll do synthetic translations and spot-check.
[05:12] Maya: timeline recap:
- Week 0 (this week): agree on scope and success criteria, sign NDA/security checklist.
- Week 1: customer uploads sample corpus + labels, redwood shares bench template.
- Weeks 2–4: run initial bench across shortlist; produce model footprint and cost estimates.
- Weeks 5–6: fine-tune / LoRA on selected models and rerun targeted bench.
- Weeks 7–8: pilot in chosen deployment (hosted/dedicated/private) and board demo prep by 2026-06-10.
[05:42] Alex: sounds good, but need to ensure procurement has a clear SOW and a pilot budget, can you add estimated numbers?
[05:48] Maya: yes we'll include estimated hours for SE support, infra costs for benching, and a pilot run-rate estimate in the cost sheet.
[05:54] Samir: technical Q — how do you handle prompt engineering vs model fine-tuning? is the bench going to include a prompt baseline?
[06:00] Liam: bench will have three axes: out-of-box prompts, engineered prompt templates, and fine-tuned LoRA variants. that way we can see marginal gains and cost per improvement.
[06:08] Dr. Elena: do we have concerns about IP or regulatory retention when we fine-tune on our docs?
[06:13] Priya: yes we need to ensure training artifacts are purged post-poc or held under contract.
[06:18] Maya: agreed — we can document retention policies; in private deployment you control the storage. for hosted we'll provide contract terms to restrict training retention and delete checkpoints on request.
[06:28] Liam: a couple of clarifying notes on bench infra — we'll run bench jobs across a small cluster: 2x A100 for large models and 4x 80GB 3090-style for mid-size; if you prefer a single-vendor cloud we can mirror that. we will measure GPU memory, latency, and token cost.
[06:44] Samir: Ok last thing — any recommended baseline numbers for acceptance?
[06:48] Liam: suggested acceptance thresholds for POC:
- Extraction macro-F1 >= 0.90 for primary entity types, >=0.85 for secondary.
- Summarization ROUGE-L >= baseline by +8 over current heuristic system.
- Latency p95 <= 300ms for 128 tokens and <=500ms for 512 tokens on chosen infra.
- Cost per 1k tokens below your agreed pilot target (we'll propose targets).
[07:10] Dr. Elena: good — we'll aim for those.
[07:14] Maya: cool — recap on next steps: i'll send the bench template and cost estimate by 2026-04-13; liam will publish model shortlist + expected footprints by 2026-04-15; samir to upload data by 2026-04-16; priya to confirm security checklist by 2026-04-14.
[07:26] Alex: procurement will review SOW once we get the cost sheet.
[07:30] Priya: please include specifics on KMS integration and audit log export in the security doc.
[07:34] Maya: will do. any other q's?
[07:36] Samir: no, thanks all.
[07:38] Dr. Elena: thanks everyone.
[07:40] Maya: thanks, we'll follow up with invites for the SE deep-dive.

End of meeting.

References mentioned: Redwood Dedicated, Redwood Private (VPC), LoRA fine-tuning, int8 quantization, KV cache (mis-transcribed as kv cash at times).

Shared artifacts / links (to be attached separately): bench template spreadsheet, sample SOW draft, security checklist, and a short model footprint doc.
